newsitem.title: UK: United names price for BA/American deal.
newsitem.headline: United names price for BA/American deal.

text.p: United Airlines said Tuesday it wanted British Airways and American Airlines to give up 30 takeoff and landing slots at London's Heathrow Airport as the main price for ending its opposition to their proposed alliance.

United's government affairs team told reporters that its proposals would also satisfy United's demands for concessions from the British government in the related Anglo-U.S. aviation trade talks which resume in London on Wednesday.

United said it would be satisfied if British Airways and American agreed to make room on the congested runways at Heathrow, Chicago and New York's JFK airport to allow new competition in to counterbalance the British Airways/American combination on six trans-Atlantic routes where British Airways and American would otherwise be dominant. American is a unit of Dallas-based AMR Corp.
This would involve transferring 30 daily slots at London Heathrow, six at Chicago and 12 at JFK to allow rivals to introduce new competition.

Otherwise United, a subsidiary of Chicago-based UAL Corp., said the British Airways/American combination would start with a monopoly on Boston-Heathrow and Miami-Heathrow markets as well as Dallas to London Gatwick, and a dominant 87 percent share of the Chicago-Heathrow market, 66 percent share of JFK-Heathrow and 53 percent of Los Angles-Heathrow.

Under the proposed alliance British Airways intends to coordinate its 244 flights a week from Britain to 22 U.S. destinations with all of American Airline's 238 flights a week from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.
